blocks.text: SYNOPSIS

This report provides a description of the manufacturing process for OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) and summarizes the results for all the Drug Substance (DS) and Drug Product (DP) lots manufactured at CanSino Bio starting from GLP to PPQ batches. The Drug Substance manufacturing process comprises of upstream and downstream operations. The upstream process includes cell culture expansion, plasmid transfection, AAV production in cells, and cell harvest. The downstream process consists of cell lysis, Benzonase/Biolonase-mediated DNA digestion, depth filtration, Capto AVB affinity chromatography, density gradient ultracentrifugation, subsequent concentration and sterile filtration to produce the final bulk drug substance. The Drug Product process includes thawing, formulation of the drug substance, sterile filtration, aseptic filling, inspection, labeling, and storage. Release testing of OCU400 DS and DP batches from GLP to PPQ demonstrated that all quality attributes met established specifications, confirming that all lots are suitable for release and subsequent regulatory approval.

blocks.text: 1. INTRODUCTION

OCU400 is an adeno-associated virus (AAV) serotype 5-based vector containing the human NR2E3 gene expression cassette containing: a) AAV2 ITR; b) the cytomegalovirus (CMV) enhancer; c) the chicken beta actin (CBA) promoter; d) chimeric intron; e) the cloned cDNA coding for human NR2E3 protein (44692 Dalton); and f) the SV40 polyadenylation (PolyA) region as shown in Figure 1 below. The proposed indication of OCU400 is for the treatment of retinitis pigmentosa.

blocks.text: This report describes the manufacturing activities for OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) DS and DP from GLP to PPQ. A total of nine batches as summarized in Table 1, were manufactured across development and commercialization stages, including one 50 L GLP batch, one 200 L Phase I/II batch, two 300 L engineering batches, two 300 L Phase III clinical batches, and three 300 L PPQ batches. These batches were produced to support process development, scale-up, clinical supply, and process validation. The manufacturing process described herein represents an end-to-end operation, starting from vial thaw and extending through final DP labelling and packaging. The OCU400 DS and DP process were executed using the established manufacturing platform, and any process changes introduced during scale-up were carefully documented and evaluated to ensure continued process control and product quality.

2. PRODUCTION OF OCU400 (AAV5-HNR2E3)
2.1. Overview of Manufacturing Process for OCU400 (AAV5- hNR2E3) Drug Substance

blocks.text:
The OCU400 drug substance (DS) manufacturing process consists of upstream cell expansion, transient transfection, harvest and lysis, clarification, purification, concentration, and formulation steps performed under specified GLP/GMP conditions. The process is scalable and applicable across clinical, engineering, validation, and commercial manufacturing batches.

The HEK293 cells are expanded through a stepwise scale-up in shake flasks and subsequently transferred to a production bioreactor. The manufacturing process utilizes a Working Cell Bank (WCB) derived from a well-characterized Master Cell Bank (MCB) prepared and qualified under GMP conditions (Refer the MCB and WCB characterization report: ERPT-0150).

Upon reaching the target cell density in the production bioreactor, the suspension culture is transiently transfected with a plasmid mixture containing the expression plasmid encoding hNR2E3, the AAV rep2/cap5 plasmid, and the adenoviral helper plasmid. The plasmids are manufactured from qualified bacterial cell banks and purified using chromatography-based methods prior to formulation in an appropriate buffer. The plasmid mixture is complexed with cationic lipid polyethylenimine (PEI) in Balan CD HEK293 media and added into the bioreactor. The culture is maintained under controlled conditions to allow AAV production.

Following the production phase, the culture is harvested, and the cell biomass is collected by centrifugation. The cell pellet is resuspended in lysis buffer and subjected to controlled freeze-thaw processing to generate cell lysate. The lysate is treated with nuclease to degrade host cell DNA and residual plasmid DNA.

blocks.text: The treated lysate is clarified by centrifugation followed by depth filtration and bioburden reduction filtration. The clarified lysate is tested for vector genome (Vg) titer and subsequently purified using Capto AVB column for affinity purification. This column contains 14 kDa antibody expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, which binds to AAV5. The AAV5-hNR2E3 viral particles bound to the Capto AVB column are eluted with elution buffer. The affinity-purified eluate is concentrated by tangential flow filtration. To separate full capsids from empty capsids and other impurities, the material is further purified by iodixanol density gradient ultracentrifugation. The fraction containing full AAV5-hNR2E3 viral particles is collected and pooled. The pooled fractions are concentrated by tangential flow filtration followed by diafiltration using DS buffer. Following final sterile filtration, the OCU400 bulk drug substance (BDS) is filled in sterile SEBC bottles and stored at ≤- 60℃. The production of the OCU400 DS at manufacturing scale is summarized in Figure 2.

4.1. Overview of the Upstream Manufacturing Process

blocks.text: The OCU400 DS is produced in HEK293 suspension cell culture using a production bioreactor-based manufacturing process. HEK293 cells are initially recovered and cultivated in an Erlenmeyer shake flask to initiate the seed train. The cell culture is expanded from the HEK293SF-3F6 working cell bank (WCB) and is performed through sequential scale-up of the culture volume. Following recovery, the cells are expanded through progressively larger shake flask cultures and intermediate seed expansion steps until the required cell biomass is achieved for inoculation of the production bioreactor. The upstream process is designed to support manufacturing across campaigns while maintaining consistent culture conditions and process performance. The upstream process flow for OCU400 production from GLP to PPQ scale is represented in Figure 3.

4.2. Production of Plasmids (Transgene, Helper, and Rep/Cap)

blocks.text: The production of OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) is based on triple plasmid transfection in HEK293 suspension cells with transgene phNR2E3, pRep2/Cap5, and pHelper plasmids. The phNR2E3 transgene plasmid is designed, synthesized, and characterized for identity and integrity of various regulatory elements (AAV2-ITR, CMV enhancer, CBA promoter, chimeric intron from rabbit globulin gene, and SV40 poly A). The rep gene sequence consists of wild type AAV2 serotype, and the cap gene sequence consists of wild type AAV5 serotype. The pHelper plasmid is used to provide various factors for AAV5 production in HEK293 cells. During research and development, Ampicillin antibiotic cassette was replaced with a kanamycin antibiotic cassette in all the plasmids (phNR2E3, pRep2/Cap5 and pHelper plasmids) and characterized for identity in plasmids produced during cGMP production. The purified plasmids were released against the specification.

4.3.1. Overview of Seed Flask Preparation and Inoculation

blocks.text: The purpose of the seed flask passage steps is to generate sufficient biomass of HEK293 cells for inoculation in the production bioreactor. Seed cultures are passaged at defined intervals under controlled conditions to maintain cell viability and growth characteristics. Subsequent seed flasks are inoculated at an appropriate viable cell density to support consistent expansion. Cells are sequentially expanded through culturing in a series of shake flasks and transferred to a seed bioreactor to generate adequate cell biomass for inoculation of the production bioreactor. The seed train strategy is scalable and designed to ensure consistent cell growth performance across manufacturing scales.

blocks.text:
Cell Passage 5: After 68 to 100 hours of cell cultivation, samples are collected from each flask and tested for cell density, viability, and morphology. The cell cultures obtained from cell passage 4 are transferred into six 3L Erlenmeyer flasks. Prewarmed BalanCD HEK293 medium containing (2% v/v) L-Glutamine (v/v) is added to each flask to make up final volume of 1728 mL. Prior to cell cultivation, 0.5 mL samples are collected from each 3000 mL Erlenmeyer flask and tested for cell density, viability, and morphology. The six 3000 mL Erlenmeyer flasks containing the cell suspension are placed in a CO2 incubator.

a. Pre-culture in 200 L Bioreactor:

While the Cell passage 4 is in progress, 50L BalanCD HEK293 medium is aseptically transferred into the 200L bioreactor. The bioreactor is run for pre-culturing and after 68 to 100 hours of cell cultivation of Cell Passage 5, a sample is collected from each of the 3L flasks to test for cell density and viability.

b. Inoculation in 200 L Bioreactor:

A feeding system is welded to the bioreactor bag and the pooled cell seed from passage 4 is inoculated to the bag using the compressed air. After 10-30 minutes of starting the culture, a sample is removed using a 50 mL sterile syringe for measuring cell density and viability.

c. First media addition:

After cultivation for 20 to 76 hours, if culture reaches the targeted cell density (1.0-1.6 x 106 cells/mL) and viability (≥85%), cells are fed with 25 L BalanCD HEK293 medium pre- warmed to 37±1℃. After 1 to 6 hours of culture, a sample from the bioreactor is removed for cell density and viability testing.

d. Second media addition:

After cultivation for 20 to 76 hours, if culture reaches the targeted cell density (1.6-2.0 x 106 cells/mL) and viability (≥85%), cells are fed with 25 L BalanCD HEK293 medium pre- warmed to 37±1℃. After 1 to 6 hours of culture, a sample from the bioreactor is removed for cell density and viability testing.

blocks.text: 5. DOWNSTREAM PRODUCTION OF OCU400 (AAV5- HNR2E3)
5.1. Overview of Downstream Production Process

The production bioreactor culture is collected into sterile centrifuge bottles and centrifuged for a specified time at 2-8℃ for harvesting. The cell pellet are resuspended with lysis buffer stored at ≤-60℃ for ≥ 72 hours. Frozen cell harvests are thawed in water bath at 37 ± 1 ℃ and treated with biolonase to digest host cell DNA and plasmid DNA. After conductivity adjustment with IEX buffer, the crude cell lysate is clarified by centrifugation and depth filtration and further processed using a 0.65/0.2-micron filter to reduce bioburden. The clarified lysate is purified using Capto AVB affinity chromatography in a bind and elute mode. OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) is eluted at low pH, the eluate was concentrated by TFF (TFF-1) and further purified by density gradient ultra-centrifugation. OCU400 (AAV5- hNR2E3) is collected and concentrated to a designated viral particle concentration (Vg) by TFF (TFF-2) and formulated by diafiltration with the formulation buffer. An overview diagram for the downstream process is shown in Figure 4.

blocks.text: 5.3. Biolonase Treatment and Clarification

The frozen cell lysate generated from the cell harvesting step is thawed at 37±1℃. Following thawing, the lysate is transferred to a mixer bag. Samples are collected for Vg testing and frozen at ≤-60℃. Biolonase is added to mixer bag at 400 U/g concentration. The lysate is then stirred at room temperature. Samples are collected from mixer bags after biolonase treatment and frozen at ≤ -60℃. Thereafter, an IEX buffer is added to the lysate, and the mixture is stirred to achieve the required conductivity. Then the mixture is centrifuged, and the supernatant fraction is collected. Samples are collected from the supernatant fractions for Vg titer and frozen at ≤ -60℃.

Samples are collected for a Vg titer test and stored frozen at ≤-60℃. The collected filtrate is labeled and stored at 2 to 8℃.

blocks.text: 5.5.2. Process Description: Capto AVB Chromatography

After an initial WFI rinse, the Capto AVB column is sanitized with 0.5 M sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution. The column is washed with a defined column volume (CV) of WFI followed by equilibration with defined column volume (CV) of AVB Equilibration buffer. AVB loading bag is removed from 2 to 8 ℃ storage and loaded onto the column at a specified flow rate.

The flow-through is collected in a storage bag starting at A280 of ≥10.0 mAU and ending at 50.0 mAU. Samples of the flow-through is collected for Vg titer testing and kept frozen at ≤ - 60℃. The column is re-equilibrated with a defined column volume (CV) of AVB Equilibration at a specified flow rate. The column is washed with a defined column volume (CV) of Wash Buffer, at a specified flow rate.

The viral particles are eluted with Elution Buffer into a SEBC bottle containing 2 M Tris buffer. Collection is initiated at A280 5 to 10 mAU and ending at A 280 20 to 10 mAU at a specified flow rate. The pH of the eluate is adjusted to 7.80 to 8.20 with 2 M Tris buffer (pH 9.00±0.05). Samples were collected from the eluate and frozen at ≤-60℃ for Vg titer testing. The remainder of the eluate is transferred to 2 to 8℃ storage. The column is washed with AVB Equilibration buffer followed by WFI and stored in 20% ethanol.

blocks.text: 5.6. Concentration of Capto AVB Eluate (TFF-1)
5.6.1. Overview of concentration of Capto AVB Eluate (TFF-1)
container_path: 5.6.1. Overview of concentration of Capto AVB Eluate (TFF-1)

blocks.text: The AVB eluate is concentrated using TFF. The TFF system is equipped with a Hollow fiber 100kDa mPES membrane. Prior to use, the module is rinsed with WFI and sanitized with 0.5M NaOH. The base is washed out by an additional WFI rinse followed by equilibration in the AVB Equilibration Buffer. The Capto AVB eluate is concentrated to 0.5-1.0 × 1013 Vg/mL.
container_path: 5.6.1. Overview of concentration of Capto AVB Eluate (TFF-1)

blocks.text: 5.6.2. Process Description: Concentration of Capto AVB Eluate (TFF-1)
container_path: 5.6.2. Process Description: Concentration of Capto AVB Eluate (TFF-1)

blocks.text:
A hollow fiber filter is installed to the tangential flow filtration (TFF) system. A feed tube, retentate tube, and permeate tube are cyclically rinsed with WFI, determine the dead volume and perform integrity testing. The filter is cleaned with 0.5 M NaOH. The filter is then rinsed with WFI until the permeate liquid reaches close to pH of WFI. The filter is equilibrated with AVB equilibration buffer. The retentate tube and hollow fiber are drained and pH of permeate solution is determined (Table 30).

The Vg titer results of the eluate are recorded, and the eluate is concentrated to a target of 0.5 to 1 × 1013 Vg/mL Ultrafiltration is performed to concentrate the eluate. The retentate tube and hollow fiber are drained, and the permeation is collected in a SEBC bottle, and the weight is recorded.

The membrane is washed with AVB Equilibration Buffer, and the wash solution is collected in a storage bottle. Wash solution and concentrated virus particles are transferred into a storage bottle. Sample is collected and frozen at ≤ -60℃ for Vg titer testing. Final concentrated virus solution is stored at 2 to 8℃.

blocks.text: 5.7. Density Gradient Ultracentrifugation
5.7.1. Overview of iodixanol density ultracentrifugation step
container_path: 5.7.1. Overview of iodixanol density ultracentrifugation step

blocks.text: Density gradient ultracentrifugation with iodixanol is used to separate the empty capsids from full capsids. The TFF-1 concentrate is divided into multiple centrifuge tubes and centrifuged for 80 to 100 minutes. The tubes are punctured at the bottom, and an additional syringe is inserted at the top to force liquid downward. The first liquid portion of the tube is discarded, after which fractions are collected containing the full viral particles. These fractions are pooled from the centrifuge tubes and tested for Vg titer. The product is either frozen or used for the TFF-2 step for concentration and diafiltration using the formulation buffer.
container_path: 5.7.1. Overview of iodixanol density ultracentrifugation step

blocks.text: 5.7.2. Density gradient ultracentrifugation with iodixanol

The bottles of TFF-1 concentrate are removed from the 2 to 8℃ storage <24 hours, and 17.0 to 18.0 mL of concentrate is added into each of 8 ultracentrifugation tubes followed by sequential addition of different percentages of iodixanol solutions as depicted in Figure 5 .

PBS (1X) is added to fill the remaining volume in the tube, and the tube opening is heat sealed. Tubes are centrifuged at 69,000 rpm for 80 to 100 minutes at 16 to 20℃. Following ultracentrifugation, an 18G syringe needle is inserted in the bottom of the tube to create an opening, and a single use venoclysis needle (0.55×17.5RWLB) is inserted in the top of the tube. Air is injected into the tube to force the liquid to flow downward. The first 2.5 mL solution is discarded, and a 2.5 mL solution containing the viral particles is collected

blocks.text: 5.8.1. Overview of concentration of Pooled Ultrafiltration Samples and Buffer Exchange
container_path: 5.8. TFF-2: Concentration of Pooled Ultrafiltration Samples and Buffer Exchange
5.8.1. Overview of concentration of Pooled Ultrafiltration Samples and Buffer Exchange

blocks.text: The ultrafiltration (UF) pool is concentrated using TFF system equipped with a Hollow fiber 100kDa mPES membrane. Prior to use, the module is rinsed with WFI and sanitized with NaOH. The base is washed out by an additional WFI rinse, followed by equilibration in Formulation Buffer. The UF pool is concentrated to a 0.5-2.0 × 1013 Vg titer and diafiltered using DS Buffer.
container_path: 5.8. TFF-2: Concentration of Pooled Ultrafiltration Samples and Buffer Exchange
5.8.1. Overview of concentration of Pooled Ultrafiltration Samples and Buffer Exchange

blocks.text: 5.8.2. Process Description: Concentration of Pooled Ultrafiltration Samples and Buffer Exchange
container_path: 5.8. TFF-2: Concentration of Pooled Ultrafiltration Samples and Buffer Exchange
5.8.2. Process Description: Concentration of Pooled Ultrafiltration Samples and Buffer Exchange

blocks.text:
A hollow fiber filter is installed to the TFF system. A feed tube, retentate tube, and permeate tube are cyclically rinsed with WFI, determine the dead volume (≤150.0g) and perform integrity testing. The filter is cleaned with 0.5 M NaOH and then rinsed with WFI until the permeate liquid reaches close to pH of WFI. The system is then equilibrated with DS Buffer (1.8mM sodium dihydrogen phosphate, 8.2mM disodium hydrogen phosphate, 180 mM sodium chloride, and 0.001% Poloxamer 188), pH of permeate rinsing solution should be 7.30±0.05.

Based on the result of the Vg titer test, the diluted viral particle solution is concentrated via ultrafiltration to the target viral particle concentration of 0.5-2.0× 1013 Vg/mL.

The concentrated viral particle solution is diluted 30 times with DS buffer, and diafiltration is performed for buffer exchange at a defined flow rate and TMP . The membrane is circulated with 1.0-1.5 DV of DS Buffer (wash volume for Phase1/2), and the solution added to the viral concentrate. Samples are taken for Vg titer testing and frozen at ≤ -60℃. The concentrated and purified OCU400 is stored at 2 to 8℃ for less than 24 hours.

blocks.text: OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) drug product (DP) is a clear, colorless, sterile solution containing AAV5-hNR2E3 at a target concentration of 2.1 × 1012 vg/mL. DP is formulated in 10 mM sodium phosphate, 180 mM sodium chloride, and 0.001% Poloxamer 188 (PF-68), pH 7.3±0.5.

A kit containing one vial of DP and three vials of vehicle (formulation buffer or diluent) will be packaged together and supplied to approved hospitals/clinical centers at ≤ -60℃.
